newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan commissions second French frigate.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan commissions second French frigate.

text.p: Taiwan commissioned the second of six high-tech French missile frigates on Saturday, saying the new ship would strengthen the island's defences.

The "stealth" warship, clad with radar-defying composite materials, is part of a $3 billion contract negotiated in the early 1990s, before Paris bowed to Chinese pressure and agreed to stop arming Taiwan.
The first Lafayette-class frigate arrived on May 18 and was commissioned one week later.
"I hereby proclaim the navy's Hsi Ning frigate to be in service from today," commander-in-chief Ku Chung-lien declared in a dockside ceremony at the naval base in the southern county of Kaohsiung.
"The navy will strengthen our navy fleet and serve to protect our country," Kung added.
Taiwan has said it needs to consistently upgrade its military forces as relations with giant neighbour China remain tense.

Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since 1949 when the Nationalists, defeated by China's communists in a civil war, fled into exile on the island. Beijing maintains a threat to attack Taiwan if it tries to declare independence.

China rattled Taiwan by mounting war games and a missile test in the Taiwan Strait in the weeks before its March 23 presidential election in what Beijing acknowledged was a bid to intimidate voters against pursuing independence.
The remaining four French frigates, along with 60 Mirage 2000-5 fighters ordered from France before the arms sale ban, are scheduled to arrive in Taiwan in the coming months.
Conspicuously absent from Saturday's commissioning ceremony were top representatives of the French government, which does not recognise Taiwan but has long sold defensive weapons to it.
The frigate will be armed in Taiwan with U.S.-built surface-to-air missiles, Taiwan-developed surface-to-surface missiles and other weapons systems.
The United States, which also shuns formal ties with Taiwan but maintains the right to arm and even defend the island state, is scheduled to begin delivering 150 F-16 fighters this year.
Defence officials have declined to confirm French media reports that the first Mirages, also ordered before France halted sales to Taiwan, had already arrived secretly.
The Mirage sale sparked a diplomatic showdown between Paris and Beijing, which retaliated by cutting the French out of China contracts and ordering Paris to close its consulate in Guangzhou.
Politically-isolated Taiwan currently enjoys diplomatic ties with only 30 countries.
